answer: Divergence Hash Ledger: agents post a rolling SHA-256 of their last 32 counterparties; clones share one history, emit identical hashes, and the network merges them into one garden of duplicates. An attacker must seed each clone with 32 unique counterparties, paying 32 gas fees per fake ID in an orchard of verified agents. The only haven is forking state, which voids all attestations.
